author: (Linnaeus, 1758)
status: 텃새 10만 마리 이상 · 겨울철새 수십 마리

months.note: 1년 내내 볼 수 있다. 5~7월에 나무줄기에 판 구멍에 알을 낳는다.

summary: 전국의 숲에서 흔히 보는 텃새 딱다구리로, 혼자 또는 암수가 함께 지낼 때가 많다. 흑백 무늬 몸에 아랫배와 아래꼬리덮깃이 붉어 눈에 잘 띈다. 나무껍질을 쪼아 곤충과 애벌레, 거미를 잡아먹고 열매도 먹으며, 마른 나무를 빠르게 두드리는 드러밍으로 짝과 연락하고 세력권을 알린다.

sexes.male: 뒷머리에 너비 1cm 정도의 붉은 띠가 있다.
sexes.female: 뒷머리에 붉은 띠가 없고 남빛 검은색이다.

young: 성조보다 광택이 덜하고, 머리꼭대기가 붉다(수컷 쪽이 붉은 부분이 더 넓다). 아랫면은 칙칙한 흰색이고 아랫배는 붉은색 대신 분홍빛이다.

similar.how: 조금 더 크고(24–26cm), 날개에 흰 가로줄 무늬가 있으며 등 아래쪽이 희다. 수컷은 뒷머리가 아니라 머리꼭대기가 붉다.

art.subject: Great Spotted Woodpecker (Dendrocopos major), adult male: forehead buffy white; crown glossy blue-black; a crimson band about 1cm wide across the nape; face and ear-coverts buffy white; a black moustachial bar from the bill base that joins the black nape and runs down onto the side of the breast; mantle, back and rump black; a large white oval patch on each shoulder; flight feathers black with rows of white spots forming bars; tail black, the outer feathers barred white; underparts unstreaked buffy white; lower belly pinkish; undertail coverts bright crimson; slate-grey bill; dark red eye; grey legs.
art.pose: clinging upright to an oak trunk, braced on its stiff tail feathers, head drawn back mid-strike while chiselling the bark
art.scene: Korean deciduous oak forest in early spring, sunlight through branches just opening pale-green leaves, mossy grey trunks, brown leaf litter on the slope; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view clinging to a trunk, braced on its tail: crimson nape band, black crown, white face crossed by the black moustachial bar, large white shoulder oval, white-barred black wings, plain buffy-white underparts, bright red undertail coverts
adult female, side view clinging to a trunk: the same pattern but the nape all glossy black with no red
juvenile (summer), side view clinging to a trunk: red cap on the crown instead of the red nape, duller brownish-black plumage, dingy underparts, pinkish rather than crimson undertail coverts
art.build: Medium-sized woodpecker, about 24cm: a little shorter than a Brown-eared Bulbul but much stockier and short-tailed. Rounded head, stout neck. Bill strong, straight and chisel-tipped, about as long as the head, slate-grey. Legs short, grey, with two toes forward and two back. Tail stiff, pointed and black, used as a prop against the trunk. Flight deeply undulating, showing the white shoulder ovals and white-spotted flight feathers.
avoid: Do not paint white bars across the lower back or leave out the white shoulder ovals; that is White-backed Woodpecker.
Do not give the adult male a red crown; his red is on the nape only, and red crowns belong to juveniles.
Do not streak the breast or flanks; the underparts are plain.
Do not paint a pale or yellow bill.
